text: I shouldn’t look so handsome as you in the saddle, but it’s the horse they’ll bid for, and not the rider.” “Yes, I daresay—trust my horse to you!” “As you please,” said Dunstan, rapping the window-seat again with an air of great unconcern. “It’s you have got to pay Fowler’s money; it’s none of my business. You received the money from him when you went to Bramcote, and you told the Squire it wasn’t paid. I’d nothing to do with that; you chose to be so obliging as to give it me, that was all. If you don’t want to pay the money, let it alone; it’s all one to me.
